messages.text: CHANGE FIFTH ROW AFTER TWENTY FOUR D

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's article page and its grid picture, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Balls, perhaps, trodden on by one beating around like a cat

blocks.note: one who whisks, as eggs are beaten
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
Ed Balls, the Labour politician, is one Ed

explanation.surface: Something round, perhaps balls, gets trampled by a cat-like creature thrashing about.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'trodden on by' puts the politician's first name below the beater. 'around' gives A. In the changed grid, row five turns this into WHISPERED.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat has long stiff facial bristles, so something feline-looking is described as having those.

clue.text: Watch chain from fire alarm ringing, first to bell

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the alarm word forms a ring round the letter
first to means the opening letter of the following word only

blocks.note: the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
an alert is an alarm signal
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Seemingly a fire alarm's bell ringing, linked to a watch chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' gives F, making 'fire alarm' look like a unit. Row five's change makes the grid read ALBEIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An albert is a heavy chain for a pocket watch, named after Prince Albert.

clue.text: Show disgust over Tramp's clues

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word that follows is read the other way round

blocks.note: the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
tips are clues or hints

explanation.surface: Solvers voicing their contempt for the setter Tramp's clues.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's own name is the extra word, giving T.
explanation.definitionFit: Spitting is a crude way of expressing contempt or revulsion.

clue.text: Pure ecstasy smuggled in regurgitated sweet — are Met nicking?

indicators.note: something smuggled in is concealed inside, here inside a run of the clue's words
regurgitated food comes back up the way it went down, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
the run of letters spanning these words

explanation.surface: Pure ecstasy pills smuggled inside sweets, with the Metropolitan Police asking if they should make an arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ecstasy' looks like the drug but is the extra word, giving E. INTEMERATE is a rare word; row five changes it to INTENERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Intemerate is a rare word meaning undefiled or unsullied, from Latin for inviolate.

clue.text: Farcical hotelier reads paper American women left inside at end of day

indicators.note: the letters before it sit inside the newspaper's initials
the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
the Financial Times
A is the abbreviation for American
W is the abbreviation for women
L is the abbreviation for left
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A comic hotel owner reads the paper, with American women left in at the day's end.
explanation.walkthrough: Basil Fawlty runs the hotel in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers. 'reads' gives R; the row-five change makes the grid read FAWLEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil Fawlty is the hapless hotel proprietor at the centre of the farce-driven TV comedy.

clue.text: Equals those slashing taxes

blocks.note: first meaning: people of the same standing
second meaning: people urinating, 'slash' being British slang for a pee
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

explanation.surface: People who cut taxes are all on a level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slashing taxes' reads as cutting them; 'taxes' is the extra word (T), and 'slash' is British slang for urinate.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers are one's equals in rank, and the word also reads as 'pee-ers', people relieving themselves.

clue.text: Hard hole — Els redesigned part of Carnoustie golf club

definitions.note: the definition is 'part of golf club'; 'Carnoustie' is the extra word inside it

indicators.note: something redesigned has been put together in a new form, so the name's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
O is a round hole by its shape
Ernie Els, the South African golfer
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

explanation.surface: A hard hole at Carnoustie, a Scottish championship links, with Ernie Els redesigning it.
explanation.walkthrough: Carnoustie is the extra word, supplying C.
explanation.definitionFit: The hosel is the socket on a club head into which the shaft is fitted.

clue.text: Farrier's worst job — second job in the garden

definitions.note: the definition is 'Farrier's job'; 'worst' is the extra word inside it

blocks.note: the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
S is the abbreviation for second
hoeing is a weeding task in the garden

explanation.surface: A blacksmith complains that the worst job is the second one in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worst' splits 'Farrier's job' and gives W. A farrier is a blacksmith who shoes horses. Row five makes the grid read SHORING.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitting horseshoes to a horse's hooves is the core work of a farrier.

clue.text: Go through exercise halving take-home pay?

blocks.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
pay after deductions is the net rate

explanation.surface: A query whether working out could halve someone's wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halving' looks like an instruction to take half of something, but it is the extra word, giving H.
explanation.definitionFit: To penetrate something is to pierce or pass into and through it.

clue.text: "No bottoms exposed in school", Conservative defector

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom of each word is its last letter, which is dropped

blocks.note: the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
to school someone is to train them
a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A headline about a Conservative turncoat who banned bare bottoms at a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' gives E. Both words lose their last letter. Row five changes the grid to TRACTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitor betrays their side, as a defector does by going over to the other.

clue.text: Most adaptors behind plug hole with three points

definitions.note: the definition is 'Most behind'; 'adaptors' is the extra word sitting inside it

indicators.note: the slot is taken as holding the points within it, a hole being something with contents

blocks.note: the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
a slot is the hole a plug or coin goes into
three compass points: west, east, south

explanation.surface: An electrician remarks that most adaptors sit behind a three-pin socket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adaptors' splits the definition 'Most behind' and supplies A.
explanation.definitionFit: The slowest runner is the one trailing furthest, the one most behind the field.

clue.text: Amazon nature film — no intro to aerial shot?

indicators.note: with no intro, the word loses its opening letter
something shot is ruined or knocked about, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
E.T., Spielberg's film
aerial without its first letter

explanation.surface: A nature documentary about the Amazon that lacks the usual opening aerial footage.
explanation.walkthrough: The rainforest picture is false: Amazon is the online shop. The blog notes the definition wants an 'e.g.'. 'nature' gives N.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazon is an example of an e-tailer, a retailer selling online.

clue.text: Writer of 1970s' band Genesis covering single — intro from T. Rex

indicators.note: the band's name covers, so goes around, the next piece
the intro is the opening, so only the first letter is taken

blocks.note: the Electric Light Orchestra, a 1970s group
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
I is one, the Roman numeral
the first letter of the band's name

explanation.surface: A 1970s band covering a T. Rex single, Genesis being another band of the era.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis wants to be the band; it is the extra word, giving G. The answer suits either George or T.S. Eliot.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot and T.S. Eliot were both famous English-language authors.

clue.text: Clumsily type, in Excel, large order

indicators.note: put in order means arranged anew, so the letters are sorted into a fresh sequence

blocks.note: taken as written
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone types a large order into an Excel spreadsheet with fumbling fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: Excel, the spreadsheet program, is the extra word, giving E.
explanation.definitionFit: Ineptly means without skill or competence, which is how a clumsy person acts.

clue.text: Where you''ll hear classical music — Nutcracker ballet, oddly no need for theatre

indicators.note: oddly means taking only the odd-numbered positions of the word

blocks.note: you hear classical singing at the opera
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Classical music and the Nutcracker ballet need no theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Nutcracker sits as if naming the ballet but is the extra word, giving N. The theatre is an operating theatre: surgery is ruled out.
explanation.definitionFit: An inoperable condition cannot be treated by surgery, so a trip to the operating room would be pointless.

clue.text: Figure on tennis court — director's cut

indicators.note: a cut name is trimmed of its last letter

blocks.note: re means on, concerning
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
CT is the abbreviation for court
Ang Lee, the Taiwanese film director

explanation.surface: A shape seen on a tennis court, and a director's cut of a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tennis' gives T and makes the court a sports one. A director's cut sounds like a film edition; here it trims the director's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle is a four-sided geometric figure with right angles, the shape of a tennis court.

clue.text: Artist and composer missing a green forest

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the composer's name goes without the named letter

blocks.note: Edward Elgar, English composer
the letter to remove
eco- means environmentally friendly, green
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

explanation.surface: A painter and a composer, both missing a green forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forest' looks attached to 'green' but is the extra word, giving F.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was the Cretan-born painter of the Spanish Renaissance.

clue.text: Vet cut up on motorway yesterday — where she was heading?

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top

blocks.note: to axe is to cut
the M1, Britain's first motorway, with the 1 read as I
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
north-east, a compass heading; the M1 runs north from London

explanation.surface: A vet was cut up by another driver on the motorway yesterday, and the question is where she was going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yesterday' gives Y. A vet looks like an animal doctor, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet something is to check it carefully, which is to inspect or scrutinise it.

clue.text: For example BA (first class) in English covering King Lear's leading ideology?

indicators.note: the outer letters cover, so enclose, the king and the opening letter
the leading letter is the one at the front of the name

blocks.note: A1 is first-class, with the 1 read as I
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English
R is rex, king
the first letter of the king's name
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

explanation.surface: A query whether an English production of King Lear has a guiding first-class idea.
explanation.walkthrough: BA is British Airways. 'ideology' is the extra word, giving I.
explanation.definitionFit: British Airways is one example of a company operating scheduled flights.

clue.text: Works out formula -writer's configuration is not written down

indicators.note: in a down entry, not written downwards means written upwards, back to front

blocks.note: the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
the writer's I am, contracted
a set-up is a configuration

explanation.surface: Someone works out a formula in their head without writing the configuration down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formula' gives F. The writer is the setter, so 'writer's' means I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: To impute is to reckon or attribute, assigning a value or cause by inference.

clue.text: Forbidden bar for swingers?

blocks.note: the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
surface reading: a club for partner-swapping couples
setter's reading: a horizontal bar that circus acrobats swing from

explanation.surface: A banned venue for wife-swappers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forbidden' gives F and makes the bar sound illicit.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a crossbar hung on ropes, used by aerialists to swing.

clue.text: Pounds off — head to bargains with short supply

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
read as supple-ly, flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

blocks.note: the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
the first letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pounds knocked off prices: head down to the bargains while stocks are short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' gives O. 'Pounds off' looks like a discount; Pounds is a verb meaning beats.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart that throbs beats strongly, as one that pounds does.

clue.text: Ford model Torino cast destroyed …

blocks.note: the Ka is a small Ford car
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
to put the shot is to cast it

explanation.surface: A Ford Torino, a 1970s car, has been wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Torino is real, but 'Torino' is the extra word, giving T.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaput is informal for broken or ruined, finished beyond repair.

clue.text: Preparing surface to decorate trifle, finally, cutting jelly at home using string

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word
a thing cutting into another goes inside it

blocks.note: KY jelly, a lubricant
the last letter of the word
in means at home
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
a G-string

explanation.surface: A cook prepares to decorate a trifle, finishing by cutting the jelly at home with string.
explanation.walkthrough: Trifle is a British layered dessert of sponge, jelly and custard. 'using' gives U.
explanation.definitionFit: Keying is roughening a surface so that paint or plaster will grip it.

clue.text: A UFO flying low ran initially into state of confusion

indicators.note: flying about means scattered, so these letters take a new order
initially points to the opening letter only

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of the word
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

explanation.surface: A low-flying UFO ran into a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran' sits between 'low' and 'initially' and gives R; 'initially' applies to 'low'.
explanation.definitionFit: Afoul means in conflict or entangled, as in running afoul of the law.

clue.text: … model Henry''s current car almost in plastic

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word is cut short of its last letter

blocks.note: a form is a model or pattern
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
I is the symbol for electric current
car without its last letter

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: Henry Ford's car models were nearly all plastic.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Ford fits the car theme; here his name is the extra word, giving H.
explanation.definitionFit: Formica is a trade name for a hard laminated plastic used on worktops.

clue.text: Inert element of Superman's risking planet

blocks.note: first meaning: a noble gas
the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
second meaning: the hero's home world, read without the extra word

explanation.walkthrough: 'risking' gives R; the second meaning is 'Superman's planet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Krypton is a noble gas and also the doomed home planet of the comic-book hero.

clue.text: Daft brush goes down hill, top to bottom (4)

indicators.note: in a down entry, the top letter moves to the foot of the word

blocks.note: the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
a skier skis downhill

explanation.surface: A silly broom tumbles down a hill head over heels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daft' gives D, ending the message. A kiss turns frogs into princes: row five's KERMITS become PRINCES.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiss can be a light touch or graze, so to brush lightly against something.

clue.text: Ordinarily, when taken out, insurance covers against weather

definitions.text: when taken out, insurance covers against weather

blocks.note: the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message

blocks.clueFragment: when taken out, insurance covers against weather
blocks.note: surface reading: policies bought to protect against storm damage

blocks.clueFragment: when taken out, insurance covers against weather
blocks.note: setter's reading: things carried outdoors as cover against rain, and policies of the blanket kind

explanation.surface: Insurance policies typically cover weather damage once bought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordinarily' gives O. 'Taken out' works for a policy and for something carried out of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: These shield against rain when carried outside, and 'umbrella' is also the term for broad overarching insurance cover.

clue.text: From the white nose they made shuttles large

definitions.note: the definition is 'From the nose'; 'white' is the extra word inside it

blocks.note: the extra word, surface padding whose first letter joins the hidden message
the US space agency built the Space Shuttle
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: The large space shuttles were built starting from a white nose cone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'white' splits the definition 'From the nose' and gives W.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal describes a sound or passage relating to or coming through the nose.
